subject: FenixCommerce performance qualification — playbook & harness checkpoints
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@fenixcommerce.com>, James O'Neil <james.oneil@fenixcommerce.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FenixCommerce perf discovery — follow-up & next steps

Hi Sara / James —

Great to meet this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and suggested checkpoints so we can scope a qualification run that maps to your production objectives. High-level goals you stated: low-interaction latency for search/autocomplete flows and reliable streaming for checkout assistant.

Agreed targets to validate (initial):
- Latency: P95 <= 120 ms, P99 <= 400 ms for typical 256-token responses (text gen path)
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s across a single model endpoint (burst to 350 req/s for 30s)
- Concurrency: target concurrent clients 40 (we'll emulate session multiplexing)
- Streaming: chunk-to-chunk median <= 120 ms, time-to-first-byte (TTFB) <= 80 ms for 90% of requests
- Accuracy: basic hallucination regression checks via prompt bundle (we'll treat quality as pass/fail on sample evals)

To proceed we need the following from your side:
1) Prompt bundle representative of the three primary flows (search, recommendations, checkout assistant). If you can attach a small production-sampled set (anonymized) that'd be ideal.
2) A short peak/steady traffic profile (requests per minute, payload sizes) and any special headers or session affinity requirements.
3) Confirmation whether we should replay production traces (you provide) or run synthetic traffic only.

From our side: we'll share a harness template and a suggested measurement spec that includes warm vs cold runs, cache-warming steps, and streaming probes. Plan: initial lab runs next week, then two incremental runs (baseline + quantized variant).

Next steps / timeline:
- You: send prompt bundle + traffic profile by EOD Friday (Sep 24).
- We: provision a run and send a README for the harness by Sep 21.
- Joint: schedule a 60-min benchmark kickoff (prefer Sep 25 or 27).

Attachments: none in this message — please attach prompt bundle and SLO sheet as discussed.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

- For streaming, our client expects chunked JSON pieces roughly every 150ms; if you measure chunk latency you should account for network jitter (we can provide a test agent in our VPC).
- We'd like the baseline run on the exact open model we demoed (gpt-open-7b-std) and then a comparison vs a quantized 4-bit variant. Can you indicate how you record token accounting for streaming responses?

Let us know if the attached files need reformatting for the harness. Available for the kickoff on Sep 25 (afternoon PST).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-18T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed measurement spec and harness checklist for Fenix

Team — internal note with a concise measurement plan we can share after alignment with Fenix. I attached the harness template and included inline guidance below.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_harness_template_v3.zip (application/zip)]

Proposed measurement definitions (short):
- Latency: measure server-side response completion and TTFB. Report P50/P90/P95/P99 for end-to-end (client-facing) and for server-only (post-accept). Include 95% CI via bootstrapping for P99.
- Streaming: log three signals per request: time_to_first_token, median_chunk_interval, final_completion_time. For chunk_interval compute per-client median and then aggregate distribution across clients.
- Throughput & concurrency: define a steady-state window (5 minutes) where sustained req/s is sampled; record 1s resolution and compute average and 95th-percentile instantaneous throughput.
- Warm vs cold: run a deterministic warmup sequence (1000 requests covering representative prompts) and record a separate baseline cold-run of 300 requests after a 30-minute idle.
- Reproducibility: to reduce variance, pin RNG seeds where model runtime allows, force deterministic sampling when evaluating quality (top-k deterministic decode for evals), and repeat each experiment 3x. Log system metrics (GPU util, memory, CUDA launch times) with timestamps.

Harness checklist (must-have before kickoff):
1) Confirm whether Fenix will provide production trace or opt for synthetic replay.
2) Agree on exact model artifact names (gpt-open-7b-std / gpt-open-7b-4bit-q).
3) Provide client-side test agent or allow Redwood probe from a co-located agent; if Fenix provides VPC agent we'll use it to measure network jitter more accurately.
4) Confirm token-count accounting policy for streaming: do we count server tokens only or include protocol overhead? (I recommend server tokens + 2% overhead margin).

Action items assigned:
- Karthik: prepare harness config with streaming probe and warmup script; include seed control options. (ETA Sep 21)
- Marissa: finalize measurement sheet and bootstrapping script for P99 CI; coordinate run windows. (ETA Sep 22)
- Alex: confirm kickoff time with Fenix and request production trace if available. (ETA Sep 19)

Notes on variance control: recommend running each scenario on a reserved node pool (Dedicated or isolated test instance) to avoid noisy neighbors. For quantized variant, measure both throughput and tail latency separately since quantization can affect decode time distribution.

—Marissa
Principal Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sara / James — thanks for the prompt bundle and SLO sheet, appreciate the traffic clarifications. Summarizing what we agreed and the immediate next steps so nothing falls through the cracks:

Agreed technical approach:
- Baseline: gpt-open-7b-std, warm runs + cold-run baseline, reproducibility repeats x3.
- Comparison: gpt-open-7b-4bit-q (quantized). Separate runs for throughput and tail latency.
- Streaming probes: measure TTFB, median chunk interval, and per-client chunk jitter. We'll use your VPC test agent if you can provide it; otherwise Redwood will spin a co-located probe in us-west.

Deliverables & owners (short):
- Fenix (Sara): confirm whether you'll provide production trace export or want synthetic replay. Share the VPC test agent access if available. (ETA: EOD Sep 24)
- Karthik: harness config + warmup script + seed control flag. (ETA: Sep 21)
- Marissa: finalized measurement sheet, CI bootstrapping, and run orchestration plan. (ETA: Sep 22)
- Alex: schedule kickoff for Sep 25 14:00 PST and provision the test pool in Redwood Dedicated for the runs. I'll create a HubSpot log and a shared Drive folder with run artifacts.

I've added a drive folder and HubSpot link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-fenix-benchmark and https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890.

Thanks — looking forward to the trial.
